question.text: Regarding auditor appointment for a Category III AIF, which statement is CORRECT?

answer.text: Only a statutory audit is required; PPM audit and internal audit are optional.
PPM audit is required only at the time of fund launch and not thereafter.
Annual audit is required only if fund corpus exceeds INR 500 crore.
Books of accounts must be audited annually by a qualified auditor AND a separate PPM audit must be performed each year by a CA or CS.

explanation.text: The Logic: AIF regulations require: (a) annual audit of books of accounts by a qualified auditor (statutory audit), and (b) separate PPM audit to be performed each year by a Chartered Accountant or Company Secretary (mandatory PPM annual audit, not just at launch). Internal audits are additionally common. All three audit types serve different compliance objectives — statutory audit for financials, PPM audit for disclosure-consistency, internal audit for operational risk. The Trap: Options A, B, C all weaken the regime. The common trap is thinking PPM audit is one-time — it's annual. Cross-Exam Context: XIX-C, XIX-D test the same tri-audit framework. Compliance exams (III-A, III-C) test audit-report scope. XXI-B (PM) has a different audit regime.
